text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

SIR HENRY PARKES was born in 1815. He migrated to Australia from England. He was a journalist and poet, who went on to become Premier of NSW. He is remembered with the town of Parkes in Central New South Wales bearing his name.
JAMES BUTLER HICKOCK, better known in the history of the Wild West as WILD BILL HICKOCK, was born on this day in 1837.
Horror film actor VINCENT PRICE was born in 1911. He became famous as the silver screen's greatest villan. His movies included 'House of Wax', 'Dr Phibes" and more recently 'Edward Scissorhands'.
British actor CHRISTOPHER LEE was born in 1922. He was famous for horror films and in particular playing vampires.
American former Secretary of State HENRY KISSINGER was born in 1923. He won a Nobel Peace Prize for his part in ending the Vietnam War.
American Actor LOU GOSSETT Junior was born in 1936. He won an Oscar for his role as the sergeant in the film 'An Officer and a Gentleman'.
Australian television anchor MIKE GIBSON was born in 1940. 'GIBBO' first gained fame as one of the hosts on Channel Nine's Wide World of Sports, and later moved to Ten's 'Good Morning Australia'.

British singer CILLA BLACK (PRISCILLA WHITE) was born in 1943. She was signed by talent scout BRIAN EPSTEIN when she was a cloakroom attendant at the Cavern Club. From 1963 to 1974 CILLA had elevent top ten hits. They included "Anyone Who Had A Heart" (1964), "You're My World" (1964), "You've Lost That Loving Feeling" (1965) and "Something Tells Me" (1971).

New Zealand singer and guitarist NEIL FINN was born in 1958. He joined the successful 'Split Enz' band in 1977. A founding member of the band was NEIL's older brother TIM. Their first hit was "I Got You" (1980). When TIM left the group in 1985 NEIL formed 'Crowded House'. Their hits included "Don't Dream It's Over" (1987) and "Something So Strong" (1987).
Australian tennis player PAT CASH was born in 1965.
** EVENTS **
1703 : TSAR PETER The Great of Russia names St Petersburg
the new capital of Russia.
1900 : Belgium became the first country to elect a
government based on proportional representation.
1905 : The Japanese navy virtually sank the entire
Russian Baltic fleet in the straits of Tsushima in the Sea of Japan. It was the first major victory by an eastern country over a European one.
1941 : The German battleship 'Bismarck' was sunk by the
Royal Navy during World War Two.
1951 : The Chinese Communists forced the DALAI LAMA,
Tibet's god king, to surrender control of his region's foreign affairs and its army to Beijing.
1958 : Rock and Roll star JERRY LEE LEWIS arrived in
London for a tour, and revealed that he'd married his 13 year old cousin MYRA. The marriage was legal in his home state in America, but caused uproar in Britain and elsewhere.
1967 : Australians voted overwhelmingly to allow
Aborigines constitutional recognition. That allowed Aborigines the same rights as other Australian citizens and gave control of Aboriginal affairs to the Federal Government.
1977 : Punk rock band 'The Sex Pistols' released its
controversial single 'God Save Queen'.
1985 : Up to 20,000 people were killed when a typhoon hit
Bangladesh.
1988 : A Canadian man was acquitted of murdering his

mother on the grounds that he was sleepwalking at the time. The jury accepted his claim that he was asleep when he drove 22 kilometres to his mothers' house, hit her with an iron bar and then stabbed her.
1990 : Soviet citizens went on a massive buying spree
after the Kremlin announced that food prices were about to be doubled. MIKHAIL GORBACHEV appeared on television to urge the population to remain calm.
1992 : Plans to deploy NATO troops in Yugoslavia were
finally agreed to by the NATO countries.
